links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and adherence to diagnostic and treatment guidelines on real abdominal cases
links.effect: LLMs did not diagnose accurately across all pathologies, performed significantly worse than physicians on average, followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and could not interpret laboratory results.
links.quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians on average), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

links.outcome: LLM instruction following and sensitivity to quantity and order of input information
links.effect: LLMs often failed to follow instructions and were sensitive to both the quantity and order of information, limiting workflow integration.
links.quote: Furthermore, we move beyond diagnostic accuracy and demonstrate that they cannot be easily integrated into existing workflows because they often fail to follow instructions and are sensitive to both the quantity and order of information.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLMs in a simulated realistic clinical decision-making workflow (information gathering, ordering tests) on real-world EHR cases rather than exam-style questions

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs across 2,400 real patient cases extracted from MIMIC-IV in a simulated clinical decision-making setting, measuring diagnostic accuracy, guideline adherence, and instruction-following without testing a specific organizational deployment safeguard.
